basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 29.' and it opens '(Vers. 29.) Et ecce egressus est frater ejus, et dixit, ut quid divisa est propter te'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 29.) Et ecce egressus est frater ejus, et dixit, ut quid divisa est propter te maceria? Et vocavit nomen ejus Phares. Pro maceria, divisionem Aquila et Symmachus transtulerunt, quod Hebraice dicitur, PHARES (פרץ). Ab eo igitur, quod diviserit membranulam secundarum [Al. secundinarum], divisionis nomen accepit. Unde et Pharisaei, qui se quasi justos a populo separaverant, divisi appellabantur.
